_note: Transcribed from player_aid/LoH_FateSheet.pdf 'Wound Table'.
Severity order (worst to mildest): Killed > Gravely > Severely > Badly >
Flesh Wound > Just a Scratch. Confirmed three separate ways: the Fate
Sheet's own recovery multipliers (Gravely x3 recovers slowest = worst,
Badly x8 recovers fastest of the three convalescent levels), the Rules
Summary's Duel entry ('unless killed/gravely wounded' skips the second
pistol shot — only makes sense if Gravely is at least as bad as Killed-
adjacent), and the Comrades in Arms 'Save Comrade' example ('gravely
wounded becomes severely').
Flesh Wound and Just a Scratch do NOT cause convalescence or Absence —
they are immediate stat hits with no recovery roll, unlike the three
'big' wounds.
'health' uses dice notation ('1d10÷3▼') exactly like domain/rng.ts
formulas, applied the same way; a plain number means a flat loss.
The duel-specific '+10 to 2D10' (when the loser's card end pointed 'to
Wound') is applied by the caller before this lookup, not baked into the
ranges — the ranges below are the plain (non-duel) Battle Event table.
The Overrun-card-specific prisoner sub-roll ('If due to Overrun Battle
Card, roll 2D10: 1 thru N -> prisoner; else carried from field') is
Battle Event logic (M6), not a data-table concern, so it is not encoded
here — only the resulting G/E/H/S deltas per level are.
Duels ignore S, G and E from this table entirely (booklet: 'Ignore S, G,
E from Wound Table') — the caller applies duel-specific Glory/Standing
effects instead and only uses this table's Health loss.
